summary: Regression testing of iteration-2 fixes for LogistiPro (Django + React). Backend: existing suite (49 cases) 48 passed / 1 failed + new regression suite /app/backend/tests/test_regression_iter3.py (25 cases) 23 passed / 2 failed. Verified FIXED: DST/REQ number generation via next_number() (no more UNIQUE collision), 404 JSON {detail:'Data tidak ditemukan'} for missing pk on products/warehouses/requests/distributions, 400 on incomplete POST bodies (products/requests/stocks-transaction/distributions), distribution status validation (invalid status -> 400, backward transition -> 400, prepared->in_transit->arrived->completed OK and request becomes 'completed'), admin notification fan-out to is_staff/profile-role admins, all 12 export combos (stock/requests/distributions/stock_transactions x csv/excel/pdf) return correct content-types. Frontend verified FIXED: Modal closes with X, backdrop click AND Escape; /barang deactivate shows 'Nonaktif' + 'Aktifkan' and re-activate restores 'Nonaktifkan'; /profil inputs styled (border 1px, padding 11px) and update saves ('Profil diperbarui'); /stok out with excessive qty shows 'Stok tidak mencukupi' toast and IN transaction works; admin sidebar 14 menus + 2 charts + stats; user role sees only 5 menus and /barang,/pengguna,/aktivitas redirect to /dashboard; laporan CSV/Excel/PDF downloads work; Detail buttons navigate; distribution status buttons update timeline. NEW CRITICAL BUG: any POST that includes a date field (needed_date on /api/requests, estimated_arrival on /api/distributions) returns HTTP 500 (AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'isoformat') AFTER the row is committed - so the record IS created but the UI shows 'Request failed with status code 500' and the modal stays open; retrying returns 400 'Distribusi sudah dibuat'.

critical.issue: HTTP 500 AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'isoformat'. request_json()/distribution_json() are called on the freshly created in-memory instance whose date field still holds the raw string from the JSON payload (Django does not coerce on create). The transaction has already committed, so the request/distribution IS persisted while the client gets a 500 -> duplicated/orphan rows and users repeatedly retry. Verified in DB: DST-2026-0006 & DST-2026-0010 exist with estimated_arrival set although the API answered 500. Fix: parse dates with datetime.date.fromisoformat (return 400 on bad format) before create, or refresh_from_db()/re-fetch before serializing.

minor.issue: No date-format validation at all; an invalid date string ('2026-13-45') would reach the DB layer instead of returning 400.

Catches only DoesNotExist/KeyError/ValueError/TypeError; AttributeError (the bug above) and IntegrityError in other views still surface as Django 500 debug HTML. Also DEBUG appears enabled - 500 responses return full HTML tracebacks to the public URL.

ui_bugs.component: Requests create modal / RequestDetail 'Buat distribusi' modal
ui_bugs.issue: Filling 'Tanggal kebutuhan' or 'Estimasi tiba' makes the save fail with a raw axios toast 'Request failed with status code 500' (backend bug above). Modal stays open and a retry gives 'Distribusi sudah dibuat' even though the record was created.
Error toasts print the raw axios message instead of the backend 'detail' field for 5xx responses - user-hostile.
Still native browser date picker rendering US mm/dd/yyyy instead of the shadcn calendar / Indonesian locale.

integration_issues.flow: Notifications mark-all (still not fixed from iteration_2)
integration_issues.issue: After 'Tandai semua dibaca' on /notifikasi the DB unread count is 0 but the topbar bell badge still shows the old value (27) until a route change or the 30s poll. Topbar loads notifications only on location.pathname change; the page-level markAll does not invalidate that state (needs shared context/event).
GET /api/auth/me still fired twice on cold load, both 401 for anonymous visitors (console errors).

issues: Inputs now correctly styled - previous issue resolved
Toasts still overlay the notification bell / user block area at 1920px

action_items: FIX CRITICAL: coerce needed_date / estimated_arrival to date objects (date.fromisoformat, 400 on invalid) or re-fetch the object before calling request_json/distribution_json; ensure no row is persisted when the response is an error.
Add AttributeError/generic Exception handling in catch_errors returning JSON 500 and disable DEBUG HTML tracebacks on the public URL.
Show backend 'detail' text in error toasts instead of 'Request failed with status code 500'.
Refresh the topbar unread badge right after 'Tandai semua dibaca' (shared notification context or callback).
Optional: replace native date inputs with the app's calendar component for id-ID formatting.
critical_code_review_comments: views.py is still ~980 lines mixing auth/CRUD/workflow/reporting - split into modules.

Serializing freshly-created model instances without refresh_from_db is unsafe for any typed field fed from raw JSON; this is the same class of bug as the previous 500s and will recur for other date/decimal fields.
Mutations still index raw JSON (data['warehouse_id']) with no schema validation layer; catch_errors only masks the common cases.
next_number() scans all rows in Python on every insert - acceptable at demo scale but O(n) and still racy without select_for_update; the IntegrityError->409 retry hint is not actually retried.

success_rate.backend: 96% (71/74 cases across both suites; all failures caused by the single date-serialization bug)
success_rate.frontend: 88% (all pages, CRUD, guards, exports, modal-close, product reactivate, profile styling OK; request/distribution creation with a date shows 500, notif badge stale)

rca_of_the_issue: In requests_api and distributions_api the object is created inside transaction.atomic() with needed_date/estimated_arrival taken directly from the JSON payload (a 'YYYY-MM-DD' string). After the block commits, request_json()/distribution_json() call r.needed_date.isoformat() / d.estimated_arrival.isoformat() on the still-string attribute -> AttributeError -> Django 500 (catch_errors does not catch AttributeError). Because the commit already happened, the row exists in the DB while the client sees an error (verified: DST-2026-0010 for REQ-2026-0032 persisted after a 500). Reproduce: POST /api/distributions {request_id, estimated_arrival:'2026-08-01'} or fill the date field in the UI modal. Mitigation: parse to datetime.date before create (400 on ValueError) or re-fetch the instance before serialization.
